text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic receives highest national decoration during visit to Turkey.
- "We believe there is a great future before Turkey and we are pleased because many of us see Turkey as our second homeland," Izetbegovic says.
- Leaders of four main religions in Bosnia meet to form inter-religious council and call for cooperation and condemn hatred, revenge and violation of right of refugees to return.
- More than 1.3 million voters have registered so far for the September municipal elections, Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) says.
- Bosnian company Unis Holding signs agreement with Swiss Air to serve as its representative in Bosnia. Swiss Air will offer three scheduled flights a week from Sarajevo to Zurich.

- If Federal Republic of Yugoslavia does not establish diplomatic relations with Bosnia immediately, as it was agreed recently in Sintra, Portugal, it could again face some kind of international sanctions, a diplomat says.

- If the international donors' conference for reconstruction of Bosnia scheduled this month does not take place on time, Bosnia will face social unrest, says Sulejman Hrle, president of main trade union. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
